rows.selection_reason: The existing evidence is sparse, so this experiment tests the baseline multimodal approach with standard encoders (scvi_n200, resnet50) and weighted fusion, which isolates the impact of combining RNA and image data. It clarifies whether multimodal modeling outperforms single-modality baselines, a critical design choice. This is the best use of the first experiment as it addresses a high-impact question without overcomplicating the setup.

The existing evidence shows that config_001 (multimodal, multiprofile, scvi_n200, resnet50, avgpool, weighted) achieves 0.6776 validation accuracy. This experiment tests replacing avgpool with transformer aggregation while keeping other components identical. It isolates the impact of aggregation method on performance, a critical design choice. Since transformer aggregation could capture more complex interactions than avgpool, this test clarifies whether advanced aggregation improves results without changing multiple factors. It balances exploration of key components with exploitation of the current multimodal/multiprofile baseline.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation (config_022) outperforms avgpool (config_001). This experiment tests whether changing the fusion method from weighted to concat (while keeping RNA/image encoders, aggregation, and profile settings identical to config_022) impacts performance. It isolates the effect of fusion strategy, a critical design choice, and builds on the promising direction of transformer aggregation.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (config_022) outperform avgpool and concat. This experiment tests whether replacing the image encoder (resnet50 → imagenet_vit_l) while retaining the proven aggregation/fusion strategy improves performance. It isolates the impact of the image encoder, a critical design choice, without altering multiple factors simultaneously.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder and transformer aggregation (config_041) achieves the highest validation accuracy. This experiment tests whether switching the RNA encoder from scvi_n200 to scgpt (while keeping image encoder, aggregation, and fusion unchanged) could further improve performance. It isolates the effect of RNA encoder choice, a key design decision, and builds on the strong evidence for the current best setup.

Existing evidence shows that using imagenet_vit_l image encoder with transformer aggregation achieves high accuracy (config_041). This experiment tests whether switching to pca_n2000 RNA encoder and concat fusion (while keeping image encoder and aggregation the same) could improve performance, isolating the impact of RNA encoder and fusion method. This balances exploitation of strong image encoder choices with exploration of RNA encoder and fusion variations.

Existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation (config_041, accuracy 0.725) outperforms avgpool (config_001, 0.678). This experiment tests whether the choice of aggregation method (transformer vs. avgpool) is critical by keeping RNA encoder (scvi_n200), image encoder (imagenet_vit_l), and fusion (weighted) consistent with the top-performing config_041. This isolates the effect of aggregation, a key design choice, while exploiting the strong evidence for the current leading setup.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with multiprofile settings, transformer aggregation, and weighted fusion (e.g., config_041) achieve the highest validation accuracy. This experiment tests scgpt RNA encoder with imagenet_vit_l image encoder, avgpool aggregation, and weighted fusion to isolate the impact of RNA encoder choice while keeping image encoder and fusion method consistent. It clarifies whether switching RNA encoders (scgpt vs scvi_n200) affects performance, balancing exploration of critical design choices without overcomplicating the experiment.

Existing evidence shows that multimodal models with imagenet_vit_l and scvi_n200 achieve the highest accuracy (config_041). This experiment tests whether changing the profile setting from multiprofile to singleprofile (while keeping RNA/image encoders, aggregation, and fusion consistent) affects performance. It isolates the impact of profile setting, a key design choice with sparse evidence, and balances exploitation of current top performers with exploration of potential improvements.

The existing evidence shows that transformer aggregation and weighted fusion (as in config_041) yield the highest accuracy. This experiment tests a singleprofile model with scvi_n200 and resnet50, using aggregation None and weighted fusion. It isolates the impact of profile setting (singleprofile vs multiprofile) and aggregation method (None vs transformer/avgpool), which are critical design choices. This comparison will clarify whether profile setting or aggregation method is more influential, leveraging the high-performing RNA and image encoders already validated.
